title: Irish Free State
capsule: The Irish Free State (Irish: Saorstát Éireann) was established on 6 December 1922 under the Anglo-Irish Treaty of December 1921, comprising 26 of Ireland's 32 counties as a self-governing Dominion of the British Empire with a constitutional monarchy, an elected Oireachtas, and a Governor-General representing the Crown. A bitter civil war between pro-Treaty forces under Michael Collins and later W.T. Cosgrave and anti-Treaty republicans ran from June 1922 to May 1923, ending in the Free State government's military victory at greater cost in Irish lives than the War of Independence. Éamon de Valera's Fianna Fáil electoral victory in 1932 initiated systematic dismantling of the Treaty framework — abolishing the oath of allegiance, removing the Governor-General — culminating in the Constitution of Ireland enacted on 29 December 1937, which replaced the Free State with the state of Ireland (Éire) and removed the last substantive Crown functions.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Irish Free State's territorial extent is precisely defined — the 26 counties of southern Ireland as stipulated in the Anglo-Irish Treaty and confirmed by the Boundary Commission in 1925 — and its borders are very well attested.
